beats.title: Caxton Prints an Early Ad
beats.description: An English printer circulated a handbill advertising his prayer book for sale, one of the earliest printed ads in English.
beats.note: Usually given as c.1477; Caxton's Sarum Ordinal handbill is dated approximately.

beats.title: The Vertue of the Coffee Drink
beats.description: A London coffee house handed out a leaflet praising the health benefits of its drink, probably the first ever ad for coffee.

beats.title: First Newspaper Ad in America
beats.description: A colonial Boston newspaper ran a paid notice offering a property for sale, the first newspaper advertisement in the colonies.

beats.title: The Quaker Oats Man Is Trademarked
beats.description: A smiling figure in broad-brimmed hat became the registered face of an oatmeal brand, the first trademark for a breakfast cereal.

beats.title: Pears Soap Buys Bubbles
beats.description: A soap maker bought a painting of a boy blowing soap bubbles and turned it into one of the most famous ad images of its age.

beats.title: Kodak: You Press the Button
beats.description: A camera maker promised that anyone could take photographs with a simple box, and the slogan made photography a mass hobby.

beats.title: The Michelin Man Debuts
beats.description: A tyre company's poster showed a mascot built from stacked tyres raising a glass of nails and glass, giving us Bibendum.

beats.title: Nipper, His Master's Voice
beats.description: A painter portrayed his late brother's dog peering into a gramophone horn, an image that became a famous record company emblem.
beats.note: Painted 1898-99, bought for use in 1899; trademark registered 1900.

beats.title: The Campbell Kids Arrive
beats.description: An illustrator drew chubby rosy-cheeked children to promote a canned soup company, and they became a long-running mascot.

beats.title: When It Rains It Pours
beats.description: A salt company's slogan about free-flowing grains in damp weather came with a girl under an umbrella on the blue box.

beats.title: Mr. Peanut Is Born
beats.description: A schoolboy's drawing won a contest, and a nut with a top hat, monocle and cane became the face of a snack brand.

beats.title: Betty Crocker Gets a Name
beats.description: A flour company invented a friendly fictional woman to sign replies to baking questions from customers.

beats.title: Burma-Shave Roadside Signs
beats.description: A shaving cream firm began posting sets of small rhyming signs along rural highways, each line read in passing cars.

beats.title: Have You Tried Wheaties? Jingle
beats.description: A quartet sang a cereal's praises on the radio, widely credited as the first singing commercial on the air.

beats.title: Coca-Cola's Santa Claus
beats.description: An artist painted a warm, jolly, red-suited Father Christmas for a soft drink company, shaping the way he is pictured today.

beats.title: Elsie the Cow Appears
beats.description: A dairy company introduced a smiling cartoon cow as its spokes-character, who later became a living celebrity at fairs.

beats.title: Bulova's First TV Commercial
beats.description: A watch company paid for a ten-second spot before a ballgame, with a clock face over a map of the United States.

beats.title: Smokey Bear Debuts
beats.description: A poster of a bear in a ranger hat urged the public to prevent wildfires, launching a long-running advertising campaign.

beats.title: A Diamond Is Forever
beats.description: A copywriter's four-word line for a diamond cartel made engagement rings feel timeless and helped shape wedding customs.

beats.title: Tony the Tiger Says They're Grrreat
beats.description: A cartoon tiger appeared on boxes of sugar-coated flakes and soon became the best-known cereal mascot in America.

beats.title: The Marlboro Man Rides In
beats.description: A cigarette brand swapped its image for rugged cowboys on horseback, one of the most successful rebrandings ever.

beats.title: Volkswagen's Think Small
beats.description: A witty, minimal print ad for a tiny German car broke the rules of big-car advertising and changed the industry.

beats.title: Ronald McDonald Takes the Stage
beats.description: A clown with a red wig and yellow jumpsuit appeared on local television to sell hamburgers to children.

beats.title: The Pillsbury Doughboy Giggles
beats.description: A little dough character popped out of a tube of rolls in a TV spot, and a poke in the belly earned a giggle.

beats.title: Coke's Hilltop 'Teach the World'
beats.description: Young people from around the world sang on a hillside about buying the world a soft drink, a landmark TV commercial.

beats.title: The Pepsi Challenge
beats.description: A cola maker staged blind taste tests in shopping malls and filmed passers-by choosing its drink over its rival.

beats.title: I Love New York Campaign
beats.description: A heart-shaped logo and jingle were launched to promote tourism to a struggling city and state, and it spread everywhere.

beats.title: Apple's Big Brother Super Bowl Ad
beats.description: A runner hurled a hammer at a giant screen in a dystopian ad directed by a famous filmmaker to launch a personal computer.

beats.title: Nike's Just Do It
beats.description: A three-word slogan from a sportswear company became one of the most recognised taglines in advertising history.

beats.title: Got Milk? Campaign
beats.description: A dairy campaign showed celebrities with milk moustaches and asked a simple question about the drink.

beats.title: Apple's Think Different
beats.description: A tribute to rebels and visionaries, with black-and-white portraits, marked the return of a computer maker's co-founder.

beats.title: Budweiser's Whassup?
beats.description: Friends on the phone greeted each other with a drawn-out catchphrase in a beer ad that swept popular culture.

beats.title: Dove's Evolution Film
beats.description: A short film showed an ordinary model transformed by makeup and digital retouching into a billboard, a viral ad.
beats.note: Evolution film released in 2006; the wider Real Beauty campaign began in 2004.

beats.title: The Man Your Man Could Smell Like
beats.description: A shirtless actor on a horse delivered a rapid, absurd pitch for body wash, and the spot became a viral hit.

beats.title: Oreo's Dunk in the Dark
beats.description: When the lights failed during a big televised game, a cookie brand posted a quick image tweet that became marketing lore.

beats.title: Coinbase's Bouncing QR Code Ad
beats.description: A TV spot showed only a QR code drifting around the screen, and viewers scanned it so fast that the website crashed.
